svg.title: Two ways to bring ROBIN into SoundHub
svg.text: Two ways to bring ROBIN into SoundHub
Both keep the same run record and duplicate checks. They differ in who runs what, and where.
SoundHub's backend calls ROBIN's API over HTTP.
SoundHub installs no ROBIN code and no ROBIN dependencies.
ROBIN releases on its own; other programs can share the service.
Credentials stay with people and roles, as designed.
One more service and one more database for our team to run.
Open: how the API trusts SoundHub's backend and names the user.
Jobs still need their own access to SoundHub's audio in S3.
checks the user, builds the list
SoundHub's backend installs ROBIN and calls it directly.
One deployment and one database for SoundHub to run.
No API to secure: the backend checks its users and calls ROBIN.
ROBIN's code is unchanged; SoundHub installs it as a library.
SoundHub takes on ROBIN's dependencies and its migrations.
The controller needs SoundHub's own AWS role to launch jobs.
SoundHub's releases are tied to ROBIN's releases.
ROBIN's tables in their own schema
